_about: Audited record of on-screen text a viewer must decode. Keyed by 'module::cls'. Every label listed needs a legend; an entry with no labels was audited and is clear. Fields: explained_same_screen (meaning is on the panel at the same time as the label), spelled_out_elsewhere (full word appears in another state of the item), on_site (Field Guide links the label to its meaning — nothing in GUIDE reaches the cabinet). Item status is derived in tools/legend_audit.py; GLOSSARY.md is generated from this by tools/build_glossary.py.
_coverage: Audited 210 of the catalog's 397 entries: every non-demo item whose recorded on-screen text (tests/record_drawn_text.py, 20 s scripted run) contained a short or non-dictionary token, read against its source. Not audited: 48 demo entries (they replay their game's HUD), 132 items whose recorded text was all plain words or that drew no text in the run, 7 not recordable (game-mix launchers, Testament). Audits were done by Sonnet agents from source; a pilot with two independent agents per item agreed on about 9 in 10 labels. Meanings are the auditors' reading of the code, not yet owner-reviewed. Second pass (2026-09-20): all 366 labels re-read against source by independent Opus verifiers told to refute each claim — 338 confirmed, 27 imprecise, 1 wrong (corrected here; each corrected record carries a 'review' note), 27 explained-flag fixes, 5 kind fixes, plus the game-over finding below. The verifiers also found labels the first pass missed; they are listed under 'Found in verification' and do not yet have full records.
_side_findings: Never-drawn text, reported and not re-checked: visuals/cell.py (state labels), visuals/peptides.py (mw/charge/pI stats), visuals/latingrooves.py (instrument names).

Recorder blind spot: text drawn glyph-by-glyph through a private helper (visuals/pantry.py _draw_char_col: MIRPX, PPPRCN) is invisible to tests/record_drawn_text.py, so items skipped as 'no candidates' can still hide labels.

visuals/slideshow.py::AllVisuals.notes: AllVisuals draws nothing of its own — Slideshow.draw() just calls self._child.draw(), so every recorded string (ALKALI, BOSSES, DUNGEON, Raphael, WONDER, etc.) is HUD/title text belonging to whichever non-utility visual is currently cycling. All recorded strings are painting titles and artist names, i.e. proper names skipped per rubric.

visuals/slideshow.py::Customs.notes: Customs (a Slideshow wrapper for user-exported GIFs) draws no text of its own except its 'no GIFs found' screen (visuals/slideshow.py:546-549: 'NO GIFS', 'EXPORT FROM', 'PAINT GIF'). All three are plain English instructions / a proper name for another feature (PAINT GIF), not codes needing decoding. When GIFs are present, playback is pure pixel art with no HUD text at all (GifPlayer.draw, visuals/slideshow.py:486-497). Nothing to record.

visuals/slideshow.py::Title.notes: Title (visuals/slideshow.py:318-330) is a Slideshow wrapper that cycles all 80 classes in visuals/wondercabinet.py, drawing nothing itself. Every recorded single letter (A,B,C,D,E,I,N,O,R,T,W) is exactly and only a letter from 'WONDER CABINET' — confirmed as a letter-by-letter build-up/typing/reveal animation across dozens of title-card classes (e.g. visuals/wondercabinet.py:470-501 WonderPacMan, :756-800 WonderNeon, :3961 WonderAsteroids), always completing to the full plain-English words on the same screen shortly after. None function as an abbreviation or code for anything else. '*' (visuals/wondercabinet.py:8013) is one of 12 flicker characters on a slot-machine reel animation (WonderSlotMachine) before it lands on a target letter — pure decorative filler, never a meaningful symbol. A full-file scan (225 text-draw call sites across all 80 classes) found no other abbreviation, coded-value, notation, truncation, or mislabel that qualifies: the closest candidates were a self-explanatory retro 'BIOS 1.0 / RAM 640K' boot-screen parody (WonderDOS, standard tech vocabulary, not project-specific) and an unlabeled mm:ss VHS-style timestamp overlay (WonderVHS, visuals/wondercabinet.py:3343,3361) that is self-evident from its camcorder-static context — neither judged to clear the 'needs a legend' bar. Wrapper guide_desc ('A parade of the Wonder Cabinet title screens — 70+ boot cards and marquees') is accurate (80 classes, in the right ballpark) and doesn't need to explain any of the above since none of it needs explaining.
